topic: Metals, Non-Metals and Metallurgy (Ores and Alloys)
description: This topic categorizes elements based on their physical and chemical properties into metals, non-metals, and metalloids. It includes the scientific study of extracting metals from their ores (metallurgy) and the formation of alloys.

sections.title: Basics of Metals and Non-Metals
sections.description: Metals and non-metals are distinguished by their specific physical properties such as malleability, ductility, and conductivity.

key_concepts.explanation: Elements that form positive ions (cations) by losing electrons. They are generally good conductors of heat and electricity, malleable, and ductile.
Elements that form negative ions (anions) by gaining electrons. They are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity (insulators) and are non-lustrous.
Elements that exhibit properties of both metals and non-metals. Examples include Silicon, Germanium, and Arsenic.

important_facts.fact: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that exists in a liquid state at room temperature.
Bromine (Br) is the only non-metal that exists in a liquid state at room temperature.
Aluminum (Al) is the most abundant metal found in the Earth's crust.
Diamond, an allotrope of carbon, is the hardest known natural substance.

sections.title: Key Processes of Metallurgy
sections.description: Metallurgy is the scientific and technological process of extracting pure metals from their naturally occurring ores.

key_concepts.explanation: Naturally occurring elements or compounds in the Earth's crust that contain metals.
Minerals from which metals can be extracted profitably and conveniently. All ores are minerals, but not all minerals are ores.
The process of heating sulphide ores in the presence of excess air below their melting point to convert them into metal oxides.
The process of heating carbonate ores in limited or no air to convert them into metal oxides.
The process of obtaining a pure metal by heating a metal oxide with a reducing agent like carbon at a high temperature.

sections.title: Major Metals and their Ores
sections.description: Various important metals are extracted on a commercial scale from specific naturally occurring ores.

key_associations.extra_info: Haematite (Fe2O3) is the most important industrial ore of iron.
Aluminum is primarily extracted from Bauxite (Al2O3·2H2O) via the Bayer process.
Copper Pyrite (CuFeS2) is the main sulphide ore of copper.
Cinnabar (HgS) is a bright red sulphide ore from which mercury is extracted.
Galena (PbS) is the primary ore used for the extraction of lead.
Pitchblende is the primary source of this highly radioactive element.

sections.title: Important Alloys and their Uses
sections.description: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or a metal and a non-metal, created to obtain desired structural properties.

key_associations.extra_info: Used for making utensils, statues, and musical instruments.
Used for making coins, medals, and ship propellers. It is harder than brass.
Has a very low melting point, hence used for welding electrical wires together.
Highly resistant to rust. Used for making surgical instruments and cutlery.

Extremely light yet strong, making it ideal for manufacturing aircraft parts.

important_facts.fact: Amalgam: If one of the metals in an alloy is mercury (Hg), the resulting alloy is strictly called an amalgam.

sections.title: Chemical Reactions and Corrosion
sections.description: The chemical nature of metals and their interaction with the environment leads to phenomena like displacement reactions and corrosion.
